To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CA125 pattern of rise is associated with the stage of the ovarian cancer, and that the pattern of rise is not associated with the histologic subtype.

(1) The pattern of serum CA 125 level ascent to the above-normal range is significantly associated with the stage and histology in patients with epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube and peritoneal carcinoma, (2) The pattern of CA 125 level increase is significantly associated with survival in patients with advanced stage epithelial ovarian cancer, and (3) The pattern of rise is significantly associated with recurrence and survival in patients with primary peritoneal cancer.

The significance of the pattern (rate of rise) of serum CA125 levels to above the normal reference range in patients with epithelial ovarian, tubal or primary peritoneal carcinoma is associated with the presence of a malignant ascites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the significance of the pattern (i.e., the shape) of serum CA125 levels ascent to above the reference range in epithelial carcinoma patients.
the significance of the pattern and the time of serum CA125 rise to above the normal value in the diagnosis of epithelial ovarian, tubal and peritoneal carcinoma.
the significance of the pattern in which the serum CA125 level rises above the normal range.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a pattern of serum CA 125 level ascent above the normal range, with or without an absolute value of CA 125 > 35U/ml, is a significant predictor of epithelial ovarian carcinoma (EOC).
CA125 is a very important tumor marker for epithelial ovarian cancer and its metastases.
the pattern of the serum CA125 level in the course of disease in patients with epithelial ovarian, peritoneal and primary tubal carcinoma patients has no significant prognostic or predictive value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CA125 level is an important biomarker for the early detection of epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube and peritoneal cancer.
a pattern of CA125 levels above the normal range is not a reliable predictor of ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses.
the pattern of serum Ca-125 level ascent to over the normal range is significant for the prognosis of patients with epithelial ovarian, principal peritoneal and fallopian tube carcinomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CA125 is a good marker of ovarian cancer, but it is not a perfect marker of ovarian cancer.
we can now predict with 80% accuracy which patients with ovarian cancer will have a good response to treatment, and which patients will have a bad response to treatment.
the pattern of serum level ascent to above 35 U/mL in epithelial ovarian carcinoma (EOC), primary peritoneal (PPC), and tubal carcinoma (TCC) patients has prognostic significance.
